question.leadin: Answer the following about Aaron Burr, (sir).
question.text: In his later life, Aaron Burr was involved in a bizarre plan to establish himself as the hereditary emperor of this country, America's southern neighbor.
question.clue: A long-ruling political party in this country had a system called the dedazo, where the president chose his successor, and emerged from a period called the Maximato.

swap.text: On June 15, 1813, Bol´ıvar issued a Decree proclaiming this violent end against the Spanish in South America. This decree guaranteed no harm would come to anyone who murdered a Spaniard or had previously done so.
swap.answerHtml: Decree of War to the Death (accept Decreto de Guerra a Muerte)
swap.answer: Decree of War to the Death
swap.clue: During the Admirable Campaign, Bolivar issued this Decree as a response to Spanish massacres. This order permitted murder of Spanish born citizens opposing independence.

question.leadin: This general's army was once held up by a barking dog, which was then given to this general as a pet.
question.text: Name this general, known as "El Libertador" for his role in securing the independence of many South American countries, such as his native Venezuela.
question.clue: With his ally Francisco de Santander, this man won the Battle of Boyaca to complete his conquering of the Viceroyalty of New Granada.

swap.leadin: Jean-Jacques Dessalines granted the citizens of this country freedom of religion, which had been denied them by Toussaint L'Ouverture.
swap.text: Name this Caribbean country, the second to win independence from a European power after the United States. Rafael Trujillo [tru-he-yo] organized the Parsley Massacre against people from this country in 1937.
swap.answerHtml: Republic of Haiti [or Republique d’Haiti; or Ayti; or Repiblik Dayti]
swap.clue: This country was ruled by Papa Doc and Baby Doc Duvalier for much of the 20th century.

question.text: Officials in the Iran-Contra affair used money from Iranian arms sales to fund the Contras in this Central American country. This country's Sandinista party is still a major force in its government.
question.clue: In the 1990's, this country's rule passed from the FSLN to the opposition led by Violeta de Chamorro.

swap.leadin: Name these politicians who escaped assassination.
swap.text: This Cuban dictator infamously eluded many CIA plots to kill him, including one involving an exploding cigar.
swap.clue: This man headed the 26th of July Movement; earlier he delivered the History Will Absolve Me Speech following a failed raid on the Moncada Barracks.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about a peak of US-Soviet tension in the early 1960s.
question.text: In October 1962, America found Soviet missile silos being built on this Communist-run island ninety miles off the coast of Florida. The US had just embargoed this island led by Fidel Castro.
question.answerHtml: Republic of Cuba [or República de Cuba; accept Cuban Missile Crisis]
question.clue: One leader of this country led the 26th of July Movement and overthrew Fulgencio Batista.

swap.text: The Chinese government is also looking at funding an interoceanic railroad in this country led by Juan Manuel Santos. Starting north of Buenaventura, the route would traverse areas now controlled by rebel groups.
swap.clue: The assassination of Jorge Eliecer Gaitan led this country into a period of unrest known as La Violencia.

question.leadin: Literacy tests in this country meant that most of its Black population was ineligible to vote in postwar elections.
question.text: Name this country where a civil rights agenda was promoted in the 1960s by a politician nicknamed Jango, who served as a vice president under Juscelino Kubitschek ("zhoo-seh-LEE-noo koo-bee-SHEK").
question.answerHtml: Brazil [or Federative Republic of Brazil or República Federativa do Brasil]
question.clue: This modern-day country was the destination of the largest number of slaves crossing the Atlantic in the triangle trade.

swap.text: Following World War II, Ante Pavelic fled to this country, where he was killed by a Montenegrin in 1957. Adolf Eichmann (IKE-mahn) was captured in this Latin American country, which has a sun on its flag.
swap.clue: In 1982, this country fought a ten-week war with Great Britain over the Falkland Islands.

question.text: Solano Lopez led this nation, the instigator and loser of the War of the Triple Alliance. Ironically, Solano Lopez was portrayed as a patriotic hero by this country during the Chaco War against Bolivia.
question.clue: This country imprisoned the explorer Aime Bonpland for disrupting a state monopoly on yerba mate ("MAH-tay").

swap.leadin: Identify the following about influential historians.
swap.text: This Spanish monk engaged in the Valladolid Debate with Juan Gines de Sepulveda, arguing that the American Indians deserved the same human rights that Europeans had. He outlined the cruelties of the Spaniards in his A Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies.
swap.clue: Some historians blame this person for writing the earliest works perpetuating the "Black Legend."

question.leadin: A person murdered in this colony was found after he had been stabbed with a pick several times, burned with insecticide, and sprinkled with mattress feathers.
question.text: Name this colony where Harry Oakes was murdered. This colony, ruled by Edward VIII after his abdication, freed dozens of rebels on an American slave ship who had landed on its Great Abaco Island in the Creole case.
question.clue: After his abdication, Edward VIII was made governor of this country.

swap.leadin: Troops kidnapped victims and drowned them at the port of Montecristi during this event.
swap.text: Name this 1937 event where tens of thousands were killed near the border of the Dominican Republic. Rafael Trujillo carried out this event named for a shibboleth that, if pronounced wrong, would result in execution.
swap.clue: This event was followed the next year by a campaign called "el desalojo," or "the eviction," which forced thousands to flee from the Cibao region.

question.leadin: While he was a member of a guerrilla organisation, this politician adopted the name Aureliano in homage to a Colonel in One Hundred Years of Solitude.
question.text: Elected in 2022, this politician is the first leftwing President in his country's history, and his vice-president Francia Marquez is the first black woman to hold the post.

swap.leadin: Indigenous peoples in this country rebelled during the Rupununi Uprising.
swap.text: Name this country that was ruled by the strongman Forbes Burnham for two decades after its independence. Burnham lent this country's city of Port Kaituma to the cult leader Jim Jones.
swap.clue: In the 19th century, Britain attempted to set the western boundary of this present-day country along the Schomburgk line, prompting Grover Cleveland's administration to intervene.

question.leadin: This party's founder described himself as the "supreme interpreter and director of the vague and imprecise desires of the multitude."
question.text: Name this party founded by Victor Haya de la Torre. It was suppressed under the dictatorship of Manuel Odria.
question.answerHtml: APRA [or American Popular Revolutionary Alliance; or Alianza Popular Revolucionaria Americana; or Apristas]
question.clue: This oldest political party in Peru.

swap.text: This "Centaur of the Plains" was Bolivar's chief subordinate at the Battle of Carabobo, and drove the Spanish out of their last Venezuelan stronghold, at Puerto Cabello. He later led the independence movement of Venezuela from Gran Colombia, became its first president, and then turned dictatorial.

question.leadin: This president's final re-election campaign used a jingle themed around the slogan "lo hizo," meaning that "he did" things like signing the Buenos Aires Act.
question.text: Name this Federal Peronist president during whose term Alfredo Yabran killed himself after ordering a hit on journalist Jose Luis Cabezas. This Syrian-Argentine president of the 1990s illegally sold arms to Croatia.
question.clue: Elected president of Argentina in 1989, this man was the first Peronist to be elected president since 1973. He was the first Argentine president to visit Great Britain since the Falkland War and was succeeded by Fernando de la Rua.

swap.text: Bad caudillo-style leaders in Argentina have a long tradition; for example, this guy led a gaucho army against liberalizers from the early 1820s to his 1835 assassination, and was the title figure of Domingo Sarmiento's lament against Argentine "barbarism."
swap.clue: This federalist gaucho joined Rosas's government after the execution of Manuel Dorrego. This man's assassination was ordered by Rosas, according to a work titled for him about "civilization and barbarism."
